name: Nitrophenol (phenol + aromatic nitro)
rationale: Classic protonophoric uncoupler pharmacophore: an acidic, lipophilic, delocalised anion that shuttles protons across the inner membrane (the DNP archetype).

name: Sterically hindered phenol (BHT-like)
rationale: Lipophilic antioxidant phenols reported to perturb respiration; the BHT/BHA structural family, directly relevant to food additives.

name: Halogenated phenol
rationale: Halogens lower phenol pKa and raise logP - the two properties that make a weak acid an effective uncoupler.

name: Aromatic azo
rationale: Azo dyes; reductive cleavage yields aromatic amines. Common among colour additives.

name: Aromatic nitro group
rationale: Redox cycling and, on an acidic ring, protonophoric uncoupling.

name: Dithiocarbamate
rationale: Metal chelation and thiol reactivity. Flagged specifically because salt stripping merges the metal complexes with their alkali salts in this dataset (see flag_metal_removed).

name: para-Quinone
rationale: Redox cycling with the respiratory chain; superoxide generation.

name: Epoxide
rationale: Strained electrophile; protein and DNA alkylation.

name: Biguanide
rationale:
Complex I inhibition (metformin/phenformin class). Bond orders are
          left unspecified because the biguanide tautomer drawn varies between
          depositors; ring atoms are excluded so triazines such as melamine do
          not match.

name: ortho-Quinone
rationale: Redox cycling; also a strong electrophile.
